title: Centauri: Enabling Efficient Scheduling for Communication-Computation Overlap in Large Model Training via Communication Partitioning
selection_reason: Official ASPLOS 2024 Best Paper Award; representation-to-search-space and scheduling exemplar.
sections_read: Section 2.3 motivation and Section 3 overview, PDF p. 4

excerpt.text: Appropriately partitioning communication operations can expand the optimization space for communication overlap
excerpt.normalization: PDF line wrapping and typographic ligatures normalized; words unchanged.

writing_move: Explain which representational restriction prevents an existing optimizer from finding the desired schedule.
analysis: The introduction contrasts coarse scheduling and local fusion using an execution timeline, then introduces primitive, group, and workload dimensions as the missing partition space. It separates expressing alternatives from selecting their schedule. The overview connects each transformation to a visible dependency or idle interval, and the hierarchical scheduler manages operation, layer, and model decisions.
transfer_caveat: A larger search space is not a performance result by itself. Demonstrate legal transformations, affordable search, and measured gains under matched topology and parallel-training conditions.

title: TensorIR: An Abstraction for Automatic Tensorized Program Optimization
selection_reason: Selected compiler-abstraction exemplar integrated with Apache TVM; no award label is asserted.

excerpt.text: The new abstraction allows us to effectively represent tensorized computations and combine them with loop nests, threading, and memory hierarchy.
excerpt.normalization: PDF line wrapping and typographic ligatures normalized; words unchanged.

writing_move: Derive a new abstraction from the unit of computation that older representations obscure.
analysis: The argument connects specialized tensor primitives to a mismatch in loop-centered optimization. Blocks isolate tensor computation while exposing interfaces for outer transformations. The paper then separates operator performance, complete-model performance, hardware portability, and tuning time in evaluation. This prevents a strong kernel result from silently becoming an end-to-end claim.
transfer_caveat: The excerpt is from author arXiv v2, dated 2022, for the ASPLOS 2023 work. New compiler or agent systems need their own legality, tuning-cost, and full-model evidence.

title: GhostRider: A Hardware-Software System for Memory Trace Oblivious Computation
selection_reason: Official ASPLOS 2015 Best Paper Award; scoped security and hardware/software evidence exemplar.
sections_read: Section 2.2 Threat model and 2.3 overview, PDF p. 3

excerpt.text: Analogous side channels such as power consumption are outside the scope of this paper
excerpt.normalization: PDF line wrapping and typographic ligatures normalized; words unchanged.

writing_move: Define the protected property and attacker observations before interpreting performance.
analysis: The paper distinguishes encrypted contents from observable access patterns, then assigns compiler and hardware responsibilities for memory-trace oblivious execution. Its threat model states the secure boundary. Formal security, simulation, and FPGA experiments answer different questions; the evaluation explicitly distinguishes simulated multi-bank configurations from the prototype and tests staged optimizations against a secure baseline.
transfer_caveat: A security proof applies to its modeled property and assumptions. FPGA feasibility and simulated configuration gains remain separate evidence; neither establishes protection against excluded channels.

title: DianNao: A Small-Footprint High-Throughput Accelerator for Ubiquitous Machine-Learning
selection_reason: 2024 ACM SIGARCH/SIGPLAN/SIGOPS ASPLOS Influential Paper Award; physical-evidence and memory-system exemplar.

excerpt.text: The accelerator characteristics are obtained after layout at 65nm.
excerpt.normalization: PDF line wrapping and typographic ligatures normalized; words unchanged.

writing_move: Qualify a headline result by implementation stage and measurement scope.
analysis: The abstract links a small algorithm family to broad application reach, then identifies memory movement as the design constraint. Its hardware claim names the physical stage. The methodology separates cycle simulation, CAD-derived properties, and a SIMD baseline; the results inspect buffer costs and explain performance differences. This supports a reusable sequence: workload opportunity, omitted cost, mechanism, implementation scope, comparison, causal breakdown.
transfer_caveat: Post-layout properties are not fabricated silicon measurements. Its original layer workloads, memory assumptions, and SIMD baseline do not establish a modern full-network result.

title: Paragon: QoS-Aware Scheduling for Heterogeneous Datacenters
selection_reason: 2024 ACM SIGARCH/SIGPLAN/SIGOPS ASPLOS Influential Paper Award; complementary-factor controls and experience-reuse exemplar.
sections_read: Section 4 methodology and Section 5 opening, PDF pp. 7–8

excerpt.text: Instead, we leverage information the system already has about the large number of applications it has previously seen.
excerpt.normalization: PDF line wrapping and typographic ligatures normalized; words unchanged.

writing_move: Turn historical experience into a concrete prediction-and-decision mechanism.
analysis: The introduction distinguishes hardware heterogeneity from workload interference and motivates both using the same deployment problem. Collaborative filtering supplies missing workload information before placement. Factor-specific oblivious schedulers explain what each information source contributes; normalized performance distributions expose affected applications as well as aggregate behavior. The experimental setup states server exclusivity and workload conditions.

title: Automatically Characterizing Large Scale Program Behavior
selection_reason: 2017 ACM SIGARCH/SIGPLAN/SIGOPS ASPLOS Influential Paper Award; evaluation-methodology exemplar.
sections_read: Section 2 Methodology and Section 3.1, PDF p. 2
Section 5.1 Single Simulation Points, PDF p. 8

excerpt.text: In addition, we validate these simulation points with the IPC, branch, and cache miss rates
excerpt.normalization: PDF line wrapping and typographic ligatures normalized; words unchanged.

writing_move: Connect an inexpensive representation to independent behavioral validation.
analysis: The paper first defines a hardware-independent description of execution phases, then explains clustering, and finally applies the representation to choosing simulation intervals. It checks selected intervals against complete execution rather than treating clustering success as simulation accuracy. The comparison includes ad hoc interval-selection alternatives, making representativeness an empirical claim.

title: DynamoLLM: Designing LLM Inference Clusters for Performance and Energy Efficiency
selection_reason: Society conference report verifies award; recent service-level systems study.

analysis: The opening enumerates request lengths, model properties, and SLOs as sources of changing operating points. title: Constable: Improving Performance and Power Efficiency by Safely Eliminating Load Execution
selection_reason: Official ISCA 2024 homepage names Constable as the ISCA Best Paper Award winner. The read author preprint adds “Instruction” to the title.
version_note: Author preprint arXiv:2406.18786v1, 26 June 2024. Published-program title differs slightly.

excerpt.text: to verify the speculated load value

writing_move: Credit the closest technique, then isolate the remaining physical bottleneck.
analysis: The introduction separates load data dependence from competition for pipeline resources, so the gap is a specific unremoved cost. It next states the register and memory conditions that permit safe elimination. The evaluation preserves a baseline with existing optimizations and measures both standalone and combined mechanisms. This sequence connects the proposed distinction to correctness, incremental benefit, and composition.
transfer_caveat: Use this structure when the new mechanism removes a cost that a strong existing technique leaves intact. Preserve the measured baseline and execution mode when quoting gains.

title: Mind the Gap: Attainable Data Movement and Operational Intensity Bounds for Tensor Algorithms
selection_reason: Listed in the official ISCA 2024 Best Paper Session; selected as a candidate exemplar, not labeled an award winner.
version_note: Author-hosted ISCA manuscript. A residual internal slide footer appears inside the Figure 1 image; use the public paper as a writing source, not as a clean artwork template.
sections_read: §IX Runtime Comparison to Mapping-Aware DSE, selected passages (PDF pp.12–13)

excerpt.text: This analysis can inform early high-level design decisions

writing_move: Expose why a familiar lower bound is uninformative, then define a more decision-relevant bound.
analysis: The paper introduces two named gaps using a buffer-capacity versus access-count diagram. It distinguishes a mapping-independent limit from the outcome of one selected mapping. Validation then checks measured GPU accesses and modeled accelerator mappings against the predicted curve, while runtime comparison addresses the cost of obtaining guidance. The argument makes the object being bounded and its intended design use explicit.
transfer_caveat: A bound on tensor data movement is not an end-to-end latency guarantee. Carry the storage and algorithm assumptions into the claim and show the validation domain.

title: Eyeriss: A Spatial Architecture for Energy-Efficient Dataflow for Convolutional Neural Networks
selection_reason: Selected as a prominent accelerator/dataflow exemplar with a clear controlled comparison; no ISCA award is asserted.
version_note: NVIDIA-hosted author paper; original publication metadata also confirmed by MIT DSpace: https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/f6342515-2b7d-411c-a8ad-a9edb23dd394
sections_read: §VI-C Framework for Energy Efficiency Analysis, selected passages (PDF pp.8–9)
§VII-A and comparative energy discussion, selected passages (PDF p.10)

excerpt.text: under the same hardware resource constraints

writing_move: Make fair comparison part of the contribution and explain the accounting before reporting gains.
analysis: The paper argues that implementation results from different platforms obscure the effect of dataflow. It defines a shared spatial architecture and charges movement at several storage levels. Comparative results are then decomposed by layer and movement level, so the claimed energy benefit follows from reuse and accounting rather than a resource-size difference alone. Chip evidence and analytical comparisons have distinct roles.
transfer_caveat: Resource parity is specific to the question being answered. Match area, parallelism, technology, workload, and accounting scope before attributing the difference to a dataflow.

title: Flipping Bits in Memory Without Accessing Them: An Experimental Study of DRAM Disturbance Errors
selection_reason: Selected as a prominent characterization/security exemplar. This record makes no ISCA Best Paper or Influential ISCA award claim.
version_note: Original CMU-hosted paper, not its later retrospective.
sections_read: §4 Real-System Demonstration and §5 Experimental Methodology, selected passages (PDF pp.3–4)
§7 Sensitivity Results and §8 Solutions to Disturbance Errors, selected passages (PDF p.10)

excerpt.text: errors in most DRAM modules (110 out of 129)

writing_move: State the violated invariant, quantify the observed population, and separate demonstration from controlled characterization.
analysis: The abstract begins with memory isolation, then gives a concrete way the invariant fails and a numerator and denominator for the observed population. Real-system code establishes practical reach; an FPGA platform isolates activation, refresh, and data-pattern conditions. Sensitivity observations and competing mitigations connect characterization to a solution choice. Evidence from one platform is not silently substituted for all DRAM generations.
transfer_caveat: Keep measured hardware population, test conditions, and possible mechanism explanation distinct. Historical prevalence and thresholds are not predictions for current products or a complete exploitation claim.

title: Adaptive Insertion Policies for High Performance Caching
selection_reason: The SIGARCH ISCA 2026 report identifies this paper as the Influential ISCA Paper Award recipient; this is the ISCA award name rather than a generic Best Paper claim.
version_note: University-hosted copy of the original paper includes one ResearchGate cover page. PDF p.2 is the first actual paper page.
sections_read: §4.3 Case Study of LRU-Friendly Workload (PDF p.6)
§5 Dynamic Insertion Policy, selected passages (PDF pp.6–7)

excerpt.text: We divide the problem of cache replacement into two parts

writing_move: Decompose a familiar problem to reveal a small intervention with a measurable mechanism.
analysis: The argument splits victim selection from insertion position before proposing progressively adaptive policies. It explains why preserving some working-set fraction helps thrashing workloads, then explicitly shows a workload that favors conventional insertion. This counterexample motivates dynamic selection rather than appearing as a disconnected caveat. The set-dueling mechanism follows from the need to adapt without maintaining full duplicate caches.
transfer_caveat: A sequence from simple policy to adaptation is useful only when the intermediate failure actually motivates the next component. Avoid treating workload-dependent gains as universal improvement.

title: A Case for Speculative Address Translation with Rapid Validation for GPUs
selection_reason: Official program marks Best Paper Candidate; latency mechanism with validation and recovery.

excerpt.text: Avatar renders unverified sectors invisible in the cache

writing_move: Pair a fast speculative path with explicit validation and recovery semantics.
analysis: The contribution describes which information is exploited for speculation, how fetched data validates the mapping, and how confirmed information can fill the TLB. The failure path explains what happens to unvalidated, mismatched, and uncompressed sectors. That detail makes correctness part of the mechanism rather than an unexplained assertion.
